goal: Replace string-based argument registration and retrieval with compile-time type-checked settings
Prevent bugs from typos, mismatched types, and inconsistent defaults across call sites
Lay groundwork for runtime argument validation and structured configuration options
reviewability: Needs rebase against current master before code review can proceed cleanly
agreement: Strong concept support for compile-time guardrails and typed settings (hodlinator, l0rinc, jeanpablojp)

categories.name: utils
why: P2 because compile-time typing eliminates recurring argument typos and inconsistent default values across the codebase
Removes a significant recurring maintenance hazard and unblocks runtime settings validation in #22978

result.summary: Introduces a type-safe `common::Setting` template struct to declare command-line and configuration settings with explicit types, names, help strings, and defaults. Replaces existing `ArgsManager::AddArg` and `GetArg` calls throughout the repository with `Setting::Register` and `Setting::Get` via a scripted diff, providing compile-time type checking and preventing misspelled option names.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core settings are historically registered and retrieved using raw strings without compile-time verification of setting names, data types, or default values. This has led to recurring bugs, inconsistent defaults across call sites, and silent errors when argument names or types change.

open_concerns: Handling edge cases in the migration script, such as templated `GetArg<T>` calls and `null` elements in array settings
Managing the sheer size of the scripted diff and considering whether to split the core Setting template introduction from the repo-wide migration
resolved_concerns: Benchmarked compilation time impact from template instantiation and confirmed negligible overhead
Addressed linter integration and header circular-dependency guards for the newly introduced settings headers
discussion.author_status: Active, author frequently rebases and updates the branch, recently discussed splitting the template additions from the repository-wide scripted diff.

result.card: This PR introduces a type-safe Setting template class and replaces string-based AddArg and GetArg calls across the codebase with compile-time verified equivalents via a scripted diff. By enforcing argument names, data types, and default values at compile time, it eliminates recurring bugs caused by typos and inconsistent defaults across call sites. It also establishes the foundation required for future runtime settings validation and structured option groups (#22978). Review is currently stalled because the PR requires a rebase against master, though concept support among active reviewers is strong.
